Clump Associations you already have

Source: R/clump.R
og_clump.Rd

og_clump() clumps a data frame of Associations, such as top hits fetched unclumped from another Source, and returns the rows of the index variants (see vignette("ld")). By default it clumps each Analysis's rows on their own, as og_tophits() does, so og_clump(src, og_tophits(src, ids, clump = FALSE, limit = 10000)) gives each Analysis the same index variants as og_tophits(src, ids). by_analysis = FALSE clumps all the rows as one set, such as the instruments of several exposures together, so that their index variants compete.

Usage

og_clump(src, data, r2 = NULL, kb = NULL, by_analysis = TRUE)

Arguments

src

A Source, from og_api() or og_local(), which carries the LD resource.

data

A data frame of Associations, with alid and z, and id: the Analysis of each row, by which the rows are clumped and the LD Store is matched to the Analysis's Assigned Ancestry.

r2

The r² above which a variant joins an index variant's clump; NULL for the LD Store's t_far. Required with a PLINK Reference.

kb

The window, in kilobases; NULL for the LD Store's far window. Required with a PLINK Reference.

by_analysis

TRUE (the default) clumps the rows of each Analysis (id) on their own; FALSE clumps all the rows as one set. Rows with no id column are one set either way.

Value

The rows of data whose variant is an index variant of their set, in their order in data, with columns clump_ld, clump_ld_choice, clump_r2, clump_kb and clump_size (the variants the index variant stands for, itself included), and og_provenance() attached: ld and ld_choice (each LD Store used, and how they were chosen), absent and clump, one row per Analysis clumped (one, with id NA, for one set), whose clumps is "computed".

Details

Variants are ranked by |z|; a variant listed several times in a set is ranked by its largest |z|, and every Association of an index variant in that set is returned. Starting from the strongest, each index variant absorbs every weaker variant within kb kilobases whose r² with it is above r2 (the rule plink --clump uses). Variants the LD Store doesn't hold can't be clumped: they are left out, with a warning of class opengwasr_ld_absent_variants (one for each LD Store).

r2 and kb default to the LD Store's Far Threshold (t_far) and its far window (far_bp, 10,000 kb), which it can always answer exactly. A pair it can't answer exactly is refused by the API (opengwasr_ld_refusal, with reason, t_far, near_bp and far_bp).

The LD is the Source's LD resource. On the API Source that is its ld_store (og_api(ld_store = )), else, for each Analysis, the LD Store matching its Assigned Ancestry, one Job per Analysis. An Unassigned Analysis is refused, with class opengwasr_ld_unmatched, before any Job runs; so is data with no id (one set, with no ancestry to match), and, with by_analysis = FALSE, Analyses whose Assigned Ancestries differ. For other LD, pass another Source, such as og_api(inherit = src, ld_store = "EUR").

On a Local Source, PLINK clumps on your machine with its PLINK Reference (og_local(bfile = )), one run per Analysis. Its LD isn't adjusted for principal components, so the first call in a session to read each PLINK Reference warns, with class opengwasr_plink_unadjusted (see og_local()). r2 and kb are required (there are no defaults to take, so without them it stops, with class opengwasr_plink_settings_required). Each row is matched by rsID: its own, from data's rsid column if it has one, else its ALID's, from the Source's Store Releases' variant table; rows with no rsID match are left out, with a message (class opengwasr_plink_unmatched, count, total: the distinct ALID and rsID pairs). An LD-only Local Source (og_local(bfile = ) with no gwas) has nothing to look an ALID up in, so data without an rsid column is refused (class opengwasr_gwas_store_required, with the ALIDs in alids, and the ways round in forms: see og_local()). A Local Source with no LD resource is refused (opengwasr_ld_resource_required). Provenance's clump names the reference's path as ld, and clump_ld is the same path.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
src <- og_api()
ids <- c("OGS-00011:GCST90029007", "OGS-00011:GCST90002412")
top <- og_tophits(src, ids, clump = FALSE, limit = 10000)
each <- og_clump(src, top)                        # each Analysis on its own
joint <- og_clump(src, top, by_analysis = FALSE)  # all as one set
table(joint$id)
} # }
